articles.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
articles.summary: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.

articles.titleTr: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
articles.summaryTr: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
articles.articleText: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says - Published A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says. There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority. According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman. There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost. They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control. All settlements are illegal under international law. - UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements - Published2 hours ago Local Palestinians said that the events in al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Monday night began with harassment by Israeli settlers. Palestinian children threw stones, they said, and the settlers opened fire, killing Fadda al-Fahidat, who was 72, outside her home. Fadda's daughter-in-law, Nema al-Fahidat, told the BBC that she died from a single bullet wound to the head. "It destroyed her brain," she said. According to the Palestinian accounts, Fadda's son, Arafat, rushed to the scene in his car after hearing the news and collided with an empty Israeli settler car parked outside his family home, injuring settlers who were standing nearby. The settlers then fired more shots, they said, injuring several Palestinians, including Arafat. "My husband, when he saw his mother, was not paying attention. He crashed into the vehicle. The vehicle was empty," Nema said. "My husband got out of his car and tried to reach his mother and the injured young men. Then he was shot." She added: "We tried to gather the injured people and move them away from the settler. We brought them here. But he kept firing, firing, firing. Even after we had brought the wounded young men here and moved them away from him, he continued shooting." Nema said young Palestinians threw stones at the settlers after seeing what happened, but asked: "What can stones do against bullets?" The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle". Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat." Later, an Israeli military source said Fadda was shot by an Israeli civilian and that there was no evidence that she had been involved in the confrontation near her home. Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Israel's police force said it had opened an investigation, and that officers and forensic technicians had been collecting evidence and interviewing witnesses. The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement. Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents. A BBC team saw settlers at the end of the street where Fadda was shot on Tuesday, as well as Israeli flags flying from four of the houses that they had moved into earlier this month. In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent. The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident. Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now. It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank". The UK government announced on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank. It is the first sanctions package since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's pledge in September to respond to the accelerating rate of settlement expansion in the West Bank, which he said risked rendering a two-state solution unviable. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies". Related topics - Published7 days ago

articles.summary: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".

articles.titleTr: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
articles.summaryTr: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".
articles.articleText: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents - Published US President Donald Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel. Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with US partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese. "Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said. "We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added. Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components. The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China. But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines. Later on Tuesday, Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand alongside the country's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. The US is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of its total shipments this year. Trump then joined South East Asia leaders at a dinner, telling those gathered: "This is one of the world's most vibrant and productive regions filled with the tremendous potential." After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would". - Published6 hours ago - Published10 hours ago

articles.summary: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board
articles.summaryTr: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.
articles.articleText: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board - Published A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media. The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement. The ministry added that it preliminarily believed a technical malfunction was the cause of Tuesday's crash. An investigation by Russia's aviation authorities is now under way. Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk said an emergency response team "quickly extinguished a blaze" after the crash near the village of Yagunovo, and the area was sealed off by police. CCTV footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen. The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area.

articles.articleText: Fon soruşturmasında 7 tutuklama daha: Aynı gün ikinci tutuklama kararı - Sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere yönelik fon soruşturmasında gözaltına alınan 17 şüpheliden 7'si tutuklandı, 10'u hakkında adli kontrol kararı verildi. Aynı soruşturmada sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturmasında yeni tutuklama kararları çıktı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan 17 şüphelinin emniyetteki işlemleri tamamlandı. Sağlık kontrolünden geçirilen şüpheliler, Çağlayan'daki İstanbul Adliyesi'ne sevk edildi. Savcılık ifadelerinin ardından 8 şüpheli tutuklama, 9 şüpheli ise adli kontrol talebiyle sulh ceza hakimliğine gönderildi. Hakimlik, 7 kişinin tutuklanmasına, 10 kişi hakkında ise adli kontrol uygulanmasına karar verdi. Sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı Aynı soruşturma kapsamında daha önce gözaltına alınan 26 şüpheliden 7'si de sabah saatlerinde tutuklanmıştı. Tutuklananlar arasında Ali Kıvanç Mızrakoğlu, Didem Muradoğlu, İlkay Öztürk, İsa Yasin Sevinç, İsmail Erdem, Kazım Erdur ve Hilmi Serhan Çapan yer almıştı. Diğer 19 şüpheli hakkında adli kontrol tedbiri uygulanmıştı. Son kararla birlikte soruşturma kapsamında aynı gün tutuklanan şüpheli sayısı 14'e ulaştı.

Aynı soruşturmada sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturmasında yeni tutuklama kararları çıktı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan 17 şüphelinin emniyetteki işlemleri tamamlandı. Sağlık kontrolünden geçirilen şüpheliler, Çağlayan'daki İstanbul Adliyesi'ne sevk edildi. Savcılık ifadelerinin ardından 8 şüpheli tutuklama, 9 şüpheli ise adli kontrol talebiyle sulh ceza hakimliğine gönderildi. Hakimlik, 7 kişinin tutuklanmasına, 10 kişi hakkında ise adli kontrol uygulanmasına karar verdi. Sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı Aynı soruşturma kapsamında daha önce gözaltına alınan 26 şüpheliden 7'si de sabah saatlerinde tutuklanmıştı. Tutuklananlar arasında Ali Kıvanç Mızrakoğlu, Didem Muradoğlu, İlkay Öztürk, İsa Yasin Sevinç, İsmail Erdem, Kazım Erdur ve Hilmi Serhan Çapan yer almıştı. Diğer 19 şüpheli hakkında adli kontrol tedbiri uygulanmıştı. Son kararla birlikte soruşturma kapsamında aynı gün tutuklanan şüpheli sayısı 14'e ulaştı.

articles.titleTr: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
articles.summaryTr: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.
articles.articleText: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody - Published A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said. The serviceman has been identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, BBC News understands. The 41-year-old - who has served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police. Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, which serves as the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC). Counter Terror Policing said he has since been taken into custody by the US military over suspected national security and espionage allegations. British police previously said he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: "Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their American partners] to progress." "These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added. FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners. "Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said. "This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk." US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon said the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath" they all take. "Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he added. articles.summary: Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war.

articles.titleTr: Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins
articles.summaryTr: Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war.
articles.articleText: Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war. Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in cryptocurrency activity among the regions tracked by Chainalysis in the year ended June 2026, falling 7.9% even as retail-sized transfers increased in value, according to a report published Tuesday. The region’s crypto economy shrank to $642.1 billion from $697.1 billion a year earlier, compared with a 1.6% decline globally, the report states. Russia, which accounted for roughly 44% of the regional total, saw activity fall 14.7% to $284.1 billion over the period. By contrast, Belarus recorded 27.6% growth, while Bulgaria, Moldova and Ukraine saw smaller increases. The value of transfers of $10,000 or more to crypto services fell 17.4%, from $591.5 billion to $488.6 billion, according to the report. The value of smaller transfers to crypto services, meanwhile, rose 8.3%. These retail-sized transfers accounted for 13.1% of the value sent to crypto services in Eastern Europe, the highest share of any region studied and above the global average of 10.1%. Eastern European crypto activity by country, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report Polish crypto ATM activity grows Crypto ATM activity also increased across Eastern Europe, with transaction volumes nearly doubling from $17.3 million to $33.9 million. Poland recorded a 120% increase in ATM transactions despite a 5% decline in centralized exchange activity, with stablecoins accounting for roughly 90% of its ATM transactions. Chainalysis measures the crypto economy using inflows to crypto services, domestic transfers between personal wallets and cross-border inflows to personal wallets. The figures are measured in dollars, so cryptocurrency price changes can also affect the totals, according to its methodology. Related: OpenPayd secures MiCA license as stablecoin adoption grows in Europe Ukraine receives billions in stablecoins Despite the broader regional decline, Ukraine remained a major destination for stablecoins, receiving $12 billion in cross-border wallet-to-wallet transfers. Of that, $2.41 billion was in retail-sized transfers below $10,000, according to Chainalysis. Chainalysis also found that countries with larger Ukrainian populations, including prewar diaspora communities and refugees who arrived after Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, generally sent more stablecoins to Ukraine. Among the 36 countries studied across Europe and North America, Canada was the largest source of retail-sized, remittance-like transfers, at $359 million. Crypto transfers to Ukraine by diaspora population, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report A Chainalysis spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the cross-border flows were largely denominated in US dollar-pegged stablecoins, although the firm did not provide a breakdown by individual token. Magazine: Paraguay bank collapse shows stablecoins can offer a lifeline... of sorts

articles.title: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines
articles.summary: The Home Office has revoked approval that allowed footage from speed cameras to be used in evidence.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines
articles.summaryTr: The Home Office has revoked approval that allowed footage from speed cameras to be used in evidence.
articles.articleText: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines - Published Further problems with the accuracy of speed cameras on English roads have been uncovered which may have allowed drivers to slip through the cracks and escape fines. National Highways discovered issues with speed cameras last year, affecting 154 out of 400 cameras but, following an investigation, said it had found another fault on units monitoring roads including those running between Huntingdon and Cambridge. The Home Office has revoked approval that allows footage from the cameras to be used as evidence in legal proceedings. US firm Verra Mobility operates the cameras but National Highways said it will now end the contract. Roads minister Justin Madders said: "We can't take chances with this. "If we're going to prosecute people, we need to be confident the system is working as it should. That's why we've taken the action we have." In a statement, Verra Mobility said it "remains fully committed to delivering reliable, innovative technology that helps make roads safer". The fault affected all of the variable speed cameras on smart motorways, and a section of the A14 between Huntingdon and Cambridge as well as the A1 approach junction to the A14. A spokesperson for National Highways said that Verra's camera system had been selected on the basis that it maintained Home Office approval. The agency said that since that was no longer the case "we are ending our contractual relationship to use the cameras for enforcement". It added: "We are considering all further commercial and legal options that may be appropriate." The BBC has contacted Verra Mobility for comment. Madders said that the enforcement of speed limits continues to be conducted through a range of different tactics, including mobile cameras as well as marked and unmarked police patrols. But he admitted that the camera system will not be fully fixed until sometime next year. Rod Dennis, senior policy officer at the RAC motoring organisation, said: "Malfunctioning speed cameras on smart motorways do more than just let speeding drivers get away with breaking the law and endangering lives – they further undermine confidence in the very types of road we know drivers already have serious misgivings about." There are 4,000 cameras across the entire road network. In December 2025, National Highways, which runs England's motorways, blamed an "anomaly" in how variable speed cameras were interacting with speed limit signs on some A roads and motorways. For example, on a road where the speed limit increases, a driver may see a sign showing 60mph but the camera recording it may still be working on the basis of a previous 40mph speed limit. The fault led to 2,650 wrongful speed camera activations between 2021 and the end of last year. Those who had been wrongfully fined have been reimbursed. As National Highways continued to test the system, it discovered a further problem "relating to how some of these cameras may activate in specific and rare circumstances". It said that according to its calculations, "the circumstances in which the latest issue could occur are extremely rare, and there is no evidence to suggest it has impacted enforcement". Nevertheless, it said it was "taking immediate steps to ensure compliance is maintained at relevant locations". It said it would out further traffic officer patrols in place to monitor the sites. articles.summary: İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı.

articles.titleTr: Asgari ücret zammı enflasyonu geride bıraktı: İspanya'da yeni rakam belli oldu
articles.summaryTr: İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı.
articles.articleText: Asgari ücret zammı enflasyonu geride bıraktı: İspanya'da yeni rakam belli oldu - İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı. İspanya'da sol azınlık koalisyon hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücrete yüzde 5,3 zam yapılmasını onayladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bakanlar Kurulu'nun aldığı karara göre aylık brüt asgari ücret, 1 Ocak 2027 itibarıyla 1.221 eurodan 1.286 euroya yükselecek. Düzenlemenin yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsaması bekleniyor. Asgari ücretlilerin yılda iki kez tam maaş tutarında ek ödeme aldığı sistemde, bu ücretlerden gelir vergisi kesilmeyecek. Zam oranı enflasyon tahminini aştı Asgari ücrete yapılması kararlaştırılan yüzde 5,3'lük artış, İspanya Merkez Bankası'nın 2026 yılı için öngördüğü yüzde 3,9'luk enflasyon oranının üzerinde gerçekleşti. Zam oranı, ekim itibarıyla son 12 ayda kaydedilen yüzde 4,9'luk enflasyonu da geride bıraktı. Memur maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam İspanya hükümeti, yaklaşık 3 milyon devlet memurunun maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam yapılmasını onayladı. Sendikalarla daha önce varılan anlaşma kapsamında belirlenen artış, 1992'den bu yana memur maaşlarına yapılan en yüksek yıllık zam olacak. Sanchez: 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücreti artıyor Başbakan Pedro Sanchez, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücretinin artırıldığını belirtti. Sanchez, “Çünkü bunu hak ediyorlar, çünkü ülkemizin ekonomik başarısı aynı zamanda onların çabalarının da bir sonucudur” ifadelerini kullandı. Başbakan Yardımcısı ve Çalışma Bakanı Yolanda Diaz ise sol hükümetin 2018'de göreve gelmesinden bu yana asgari ücretin toplam yüzde 75 artırıldığını açıkladı. Zam için Meclis onayı gerekiyor Hükümetin onayladığı düzenlemenin 1 Ocak 2027'de yürürlüğe girebilmesi için Meclis Daimi Komitesi'nin önümüzdeki günlerde onay vermesi gerekiyor.

articles.titleTr: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ta eş zamanlı kesinti: Milyonlarca kullanıcı etkilendi
articles.summaryTr: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ın dijital hizmetlerinde 17 Kasım akşamı erişim sorunları yaşandı. Downdetector'a çok sayıda hata bildirimi ulaşırken, kesintilerin ortak bir altyapı sorunundan kaynaklanıp kaynaklanmadığı henüz netleşmedi.
articles.articleText: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ta eş zamanlı kesinti: Milyonlarca kullanıcı etkilendi - Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ın dijital hizmetlerinde 17 Kasım akşamı erişim sorunları yaşandı. Downdetector'a çok sayıda hata bildirimi ulaşırken, kesintilerin ortak bir altyapı sorunundan kaynaklanıp kaynaklanmadığı henüz netleşmedi. Teknoloji ve hizmet sektörünün önde gelen şirketleri, 17 Kasım akşamı eş zamanlı erişim sorunlarıyla gündeme geldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Downdetector verilerine göre Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'a ait çeşitli dijital servislerde kullanıcılar tarafından peş peşe hata bildirimleri yapıldı. Kesintilerin Türkiye saatiyle öğleden sonra ve akşam saatlerinde yoğunlaştığı bildirildi. Gmail ve Marriott kullanıcıları erişim sorunu yaşadı Gmail kullanıcıları e-posta gönderme ve alma işlemlerinde aksaklıklarla karşılaştı. Dünyanın önde gelen otel zincirlerinden Marriott'ın rezervasyon ve giriş sistemlerinde de erişim sorunları rapor edildi. Apple Pay, iCloud ve App Store'da aksaklık Apple ekosisteminde de birden fazla hizmet kesintiden etkilendi. Apple Pay, iCloud, App Store ve Apple Destek hizmetlerinde oturum açma, ödeme yapma ve uygulama indirme işlemlerinde sorunlar yaşandığı bildirildi. Apple'ın resmi sistem durumu sayfası da iCloud hesapları ve giriş işlemlerindeki kesintiyi doğruladı. Microsoft 365 ve Outlook'ta yeni kesinti dalgası Microsoft servislerinde de 17 Kasım öğleden sonra ve akşam saatlerinde hata bildirimleri yeniden yükseldi. Outlook ve Microsoft 365 kullanıcıları erişim ve bağlantı sorunları yaşadıklarını bildirdi. Microsoft, geçtiğimiz hafta 12-14 Kasım tarihlerinde 74 ülkeyi etkileyen büyük altyapı sorununu çözmüştü. Kesintilerin ortak nedeni henüz bilinmiyor Şirketlerin teknik ekipleri hizmetleri normale döndürmek için çalışmalarını sürdürürken, yaşanan aksaklıkların ortak bir küresel altyapı sağlayıcısından mı yoksa birbirinden bağımsız teknik sorunlardan mı kaynaklandığı henüz açıklığa kavuşmadı. Kesintilerin nedenine ilişkin şirketlerden resmi açıklamalar bekleniyor.

articles.title: Carney looks to China as Trump tariffs squeeze Canada's car industry
articles.summary: The PM has suggested Chinese automakers could replace American ones in Canada - but some say that would not be easy.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Carney looks to China as Trump tariffs squeeze Canada's car industry
articles.summaryTr: The PM has suggested Chinese automakers could replace American ones in Canada - but some say that would not be easy.
articles.articleText: Carney looks to China as Trump tariffs squeeze Canada's car industry - Published Canada's car industry has become one of the clearest stress tests for Ottawa as it grapples with US tariffs on the sector. Now Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that he is looking to China, where he is on a visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit (Apec), as part of the solution. But that avenue is not without controversy, and is once again drawing the ire of those close to Donald Trump. While in Cambodia earlier this week, Carney told reporters that Canada could turn to European and Asian carmakers to save its auto manufacturing sector if a trade deal with the US could not be reached. If Canadian auto workers are "not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities. "Canada's going to move forward either way," he said. He went on to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Tuesday for their second head-to-head in less than a year. The two talked of the importance of developing their relations, and Carney said they had agreed to further tariff cuts. Neither side mentioned vehicles specifically, though analysts suggest the issue will have been prominent in their minds. In January, Carney said that opening the door to China's electric vehicles, external (EVs) could result in investment into Canadian-owned companies and the creation of manufacturing jobs in the sector. American tariffs on imports of Canadian-made vehicles have led to thousands of job losses in Canada and anxiety over the future, as 90% of cars made in Canada are shipped to and sold in the US. At the same time, China has been eyeing Canada as a potential entry-point to the North American EV market. Earlier this year, Canada announced that it would let in 49,000 EVs from China at a low tariff rate, with plans to raise that quota gradually to 70,000 by 2030. The move was a significant break from the US, which tariffs Chinese EVs heavily to protect domestic manufacturing. Peter Navarro, Trump's senior counsel for trade and manufacturing, warned the prime minister against cosying up to China in a post on X, external. "Are u really threatening to play China off the US? This is offensive in the extreme," he wrote on Monday. "You should be far more worried China is going to eat Canada alive." His comments were reposted by Pete Hoekstra, the US ambassador to Canada. Chinese EV manufacturers like BYD and Chery have already been lobbying the Canadian government for market access. Last week, Canada's Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu toured a Chery plant in China, external. He told reporters afterwards that Canadians could expect to see affordable Chinese EVs in Canada by early 2027. These moves come as the toll of US tariffs on Canada's auto sector has become harder to ignore. Stellantis, a multinational car manufacturer that made models like the Dodge Challenger in Canada, recently announced it would sell its assembly plant in Brampton, Ontario. The facility had been idle since 2023 for a planned retooling, but what was supposed to be a temporary shutdown became permanent after Trump's tariffs. The sale has led to speculation that a Chinese EV manufacturer could move into the facility, after Canadian media outlet CTV News reported, external, citing anonymous sources, that Stellantis was planning to lease back 25% of its plant to assemble "affordable" EVs. The idea is unpopular with Ontario Premier Doug Ford. In a letter to Carney, he warned against opening the door for Chinese EV kits to be assembled at the Brampton plant. China overwhelmingly builds its cars at home and ships them whole - or to be assembled in kits - overseas. - Canada's deal with China signals it is serious about shift from US - Published16 January - How China made electric vehicles mainstream - Published23 June 2025 Lynette Ong, director of the China Governance Lab at the University of Toronto, said introducing Chinese auto manufacturing in Canada would be "controversial" due to fears that Canadian jobs could be lost and that the North American industry could be eroded. "We want to make sure they're hiring Canadian workers, that they are helping train Canadian workers and that they are transferring the technology over," Ong said. Carney noted there are "clear guardrails" in how Canada deals with China, including barring work on sensitive matters like artificial intelligence and critical minerals. Canada has also eyed other partnerships. It is notably pursuing associate member status with the EU, and had signed a free trade deal with the Philippines earlier this week. Just how much Canada is willing to embrace Chinese manufacturing, however, still depends on the outcome of ongoing US-Canada trade talks. Progress has been made in negotiations, Carney recently said, but differences remain. It is unclear if Trump and Carney will speak on the sidelines of the Apec summit later this week.

articles.summary: ABD'de havacılık ve bankacılık sistemlerinde yaşanan kesintilerin ardından bu kez Ulusal Güvenlik Ajansı'nın (NSA) kurum içi iletişim ağı devre dışı kaldı. İlk incelemelerde siber saldırı bulgusuna rastlanmadı.

articles.titleTr: ABD'de peş peşe sistem krizleri: Şimdi de Ulusal Güvelik'in gizli iletişim ağı çöktü
articles.summaryTr: ABD'de havacılık ve bankacılık sistemlerinde yaşanan kesintilerin ardından bu kez Ulusal Güvenlik Ajansı'nın (NSA) kurum içi iletişim ağı devre dışı kaldı. İlk incelemelerde siber saldırı bulgusuna rastlanmadı.
articles.articleText: ABD'de peş peşe sistem krizleri: Şimdi de Ulusal Güvelik'in gizli iletişim ağı çöktü - ABD'de havacılık ve bankacılık sistemlerinde yaşanan kesintilerin ardından bu kez Ulusal Güvenlik Ajansı'nın (NSA) kurum içi iletişim ağı devre dışı kaldı. İlk incelemelerde siber saldırı bulgusuna rastlanmadı. ABD'de dijital sistemlerde yaşanan aksaklıklara bir yenisi eklendi. ABD Ulusal Güvenlik Ajansı'nın (NSA) kurum içi iletişimde kullandığı çok gizli ağ devre dışı kaldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle CNN'in beş kaynağa dayandırdığı haberine göre, ajansın kurum içi iletişim ağında kesinti yaşandı. NSA yetkililerinin sorunun boyutunu anlamaya çalıştığı belirtilirken, şu ana kadar bir siber saldırıya ilişkin herhangi bir bulguya rastlanmadığı aktarıldı. NSA ise kesintiyle ilgili henüz resmi bir açıklama yapmadı. Önce bankalar, ardından havalimanları etkilendi NSA'daki kesinti, ABD'de son günlerde yaşanan diğer sistem arızalarının ardından geldi. Bir gün önce Downdetector, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, US Bank ve Wells Fargo dahil birçok bankanın dijital hizmetlerine erişimde sorunlar yaşandığını bildirmişti. FAA arızası nedeniyle ülke genelinde kalkışlar durmuştu ABD Federal Havacılık İdaresi (FAA), geçtiğimiz cumartesi günü hava trafik kontrol merkezlerini etkileyen bir iletişim arızası nedeniyle ülke genelindeki havalimanlarında kalkışları durdurmuştu. Dört saatten uzun süren durdurma, 11 Eylül 2001 saldırılarından bu yana ABD'de yaşanan en uzun süreli kalkış durdurulması olarak kayıtlara geçmişti.

articles.titleTr: Valilik uyardı: İstanbul'da fırtına alarmı! Rüzgarın hızı 80 kilometreye ulaşacak
articles.summaryTr: İstanbul Valiliği, 18 Kasım Çarşamba gecesinden itibaren etkili olması beklenen fırtınaya karşı uyardı. Rüzgarın hızının yer yer saatte 80 kilometreye çıkacağı, fırtınanın perşembe öğle saatlerinde etkisini kaybedeceği tahmin ediliyor.
articles.articleText: Valilik uyardı: İstanbul'da fırtına alarmı! Rüzgarın hızı 80 kilometreye ulaşacak - İstanbul Valiliği, 18 Kasım Çarşamba gecesinden itibaren etkili olması beklenen fırtınaya karşı uyardı. Rüzgarın hızının yer yer saatte 80 kilometreye çıkacağı, fırtınanın perşembe öğle saatlerinde etkisini kaybedeceği tahmin ediliyor. İstanbul Valiliği, kent genelinde beklenen kuvvetli rüzgar ve fırtınaya karşı vatandaşları uyardı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğünün son değerlendirmelerine dayandırılan açıklamaya göre, güney ve güneybatı yönlerden esen rüzgarın hızını artırması bekleniyor. 17 Kasım Salı günü saatte 30-50 kilometre hızla esen rüzgarın, 18 Kasım Çarşamba günü gece saatlerinden itibaren 40-60 kilometreye ulaşacağı öngörülüyor. Rüzgarın yer yer fırtına ve kısa süreli kuvvetli fırtına şeklinde, saatte 60-80 kilometre hızla esmesi bekleniyor. Fırtına ne zaman sona erecek? Valilik, fırtınanın 19 Kasım Perşembe günü öğle saatlerinde etkisini kaybetmesinin beklendiğini bildirdi. Valilikten çatı uçması ve ulaşım aksaklığı uyarısı Açıklamada, kuvvetli rüzgar ve fırtınanın neden olabileceği olumsuzluklara karşı vatandaşların dikkatli ve tedbirli olması istendi. Özellikle şu risklere dikkat çekildi: - Ulaşımda aksamalar - Çatı uçması - Ağaç ve direklerin devrilmesi - Soba ve doğal gaz kaynaklı zehirlenmeler

articles.title: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9327-26 CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today released the agenda for an industry roundtable to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9318-26]. Among other topics, attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization, margin, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. “From the outset of my chairmanship, I have been clear the CFTC will promote innovation in our derivatives markets in a manner attentive to the nuances of these markets and the varied asset classes that underpin them,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.” View the full agenda here. This meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Dial-in information appears below. For the highest quality, select the number nearest your current location. - New York: 646-828-7666 - New Jersey: 551-285-1373 - San Jose: 669-254-5252 or 669-216-1590 - US toll free: 833-568-8864 or 833-435-1820 - US Spanish-language line: 646-964-1167 or 415-449-4000 - International Numbers - Webinar ID: 165 708 9557 - Passcode: 669856 Individuals with additional questions should contact [email protected]. The views, opinions, and information expressed by roundtable participants are solely those of the respective participants and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission, its staff, or the U.S. government. -CFTC-

news.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
news.summary: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
news.summaryTr: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
news.articleText: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says - Published A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says. There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority. According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman. There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost. They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control. All settlements are illegal under international law. - UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements - Published2 hours ago Local Palestinians said that the events in al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Monday night began with harassment by Israeli settlers. Palestinian children threw stones, they said, and the settlers opened fire, killing Fadda al-Fahidat, who was 72, outside her home. Fadda's daughter-in-law, Nema al-Fahidat, told the BBC that she died from a single bullet wound to the head. "It destroyed her brain," she said. According to the Palestinian accounts, Fadda's son, Arafat, rushed to the scene in his car after hearing the news and collided with an empty Israeli settler car parked outside his family home, injuring settlers who were standing nearby. The settlers then fired more shots, they said, injuring several Palestinians, including Arafat. "My husband, when he saw his mother, was not paying attention. He crashed into the vehicle. The vehicle was empty," Nema said. "My husband got out of his car and tried to reach his mother and the injured young men. Then he was shot." She added: "We tried to gather the injured people and move them away from the settler. We brought them here. But he kept firing, firing, firing. Even after we had brought the wounded young men here and moved them away from him, he continued shooting." Nema said young Palestinians threw stones at the settlers after seeing what happened, but asked: "What can stones do against bullets?" The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle". Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat." Later, an Israeli military source said Fadda was shot by an Israeli civilian and that there was no evidence that she had been involved in the confrontation near her home. Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Israel's police force said it had opened an investigation, and that officers and forensic technicians had been collecting evidence and interviewing witnesses. The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement. Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents. A BBC team saw settlers at the end of the street where Fadda was shot on Tuesday, as well as Israeli flags flying from four of the houses that they had moved into earlier this month. In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent. The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident. Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now. It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank". The UK government announced on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank. It is the first sanctions package since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's pledge in September to respond to the accelerating rate of settlement expansion in the West Bank, which he said risked rendering a two-state solution unviable. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies". Related topics - Published7 days ago

news.titleTr: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
news.summaryTr: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".
news.articleText: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents - Published US President Donald Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel. Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with US partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese. "Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said. "We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added. Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components. The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China. But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines. Later on Tuesday, Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand alongside the country's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. The US is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of its total shipments this year. Trump then joined South East Asia leaders at a dinner, telling those gathered: "This is one of the world's most vibrant and productive regions filled with the tremendous potential." After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would". - Published6 hours ago - Published10 hours ago

news.articleText: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board - Published A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media. The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement. The ministry added that it preliminarily believed a technical malfunction was the cause of Tuesday's crash. An investigation by Russia's aviation authorities is now under way. Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk said an emergency response team "quickly extinguished a blaze" after the crash near the village of Yagunovo, and the area was sealed off by police. CCTV footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen. The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area.

news.titleTr: Fon soruşturmasında 7 tutuklama daha: Aynı gün ikinci tutuklama kararı
news.summaryTr: Sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere yönelik fon soruşturmasında gözaltına alınan 17 şüpheliden 7'si tutuklandı, 10'u hakkında adli kontrol kararı verildi. Aynı soruşturmada sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı.
news.articleText: Fon soruşturmasında 7 tutuklama daha: Aynı gün ikinci tutuklama kararı - Sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere yönelik fon soruşturmasında gözaltına alınan 17 şüpheliden 7'si tutuklandı, 10'u hakkında adli kontrol kararı verildi. Aynı soruşturmada sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturmasında yeni tutuklama kararları çıktı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan 17 şüphelinin emniyetteki işlemleri tamamlandı. Sağlık kontrolünden geçirilen şüpheliler, Çağlayan'daki İstanbul Adliyesi'ne sevk edildi. Savcılık ifadelerinin ardından 8 şüpheli tutuklama, 9 şüpheli ise adli kontrol talebiyle sulh ceza hakimliğine gönderildi. Hakimlik, 7 kişinin tutuklanmasına, 10 kişi hakkında ise adli kontrol uygulanmasına karar verdi. Sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı Aynı soruşturma kapsamında daha önce gözaltına alınan 26 şüpheliden 7'si de sabah saatlerinde tutuklanmıştı. Tutuklananlar arasında Ali Kıvanç Mızrakoğlu, Didem Muradoğlu, İlkay Öztürk, İsa Yasin Sevinç, İsmail Erdem, Kazım Erdur ve Hilmi Serhan Çapan yer almıştı. Diğer 19 şüpheli hakkında adli kontrol tedbiri uygulanmıştı. Son kararla birlikte soruşturma kapsamında aynı gün tutuklanan şüpheli sayısı 14'e ulaştı.

news.titleTr: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
news.summaryTr: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.
news.articleText: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody - Published A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said. The serviceman has been identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, BBC News understands. The 41-year-old - who has served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police. Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, which serves as the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC). Counter Terror Policing said he has since been taken into custody by the US military over suspected national security and espionage allegations. British police previously said he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: "Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their American partners] to progress." "These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added. FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners. "Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said. "This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk." US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon said the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath" they all take. "Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he added. news.summary: Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war.

news.titleTr: Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins
news.summaryTr: Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war.
news.articleText: Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war. Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in cryptocurrency activity among the regions tracked by Chainalysis in the year ended June 2026, falling 7.9% even as retail-sized transfers increased in value, according to a report published Tuesday. The region’s crypto economy shrank to $642.1 billion from $697.1 billion a year earlier, compared with a 1.6% decline globally, the report states. Russia, which accounted for roughly 44% of the regional total, saw activity fall 14.7% to $284.1 billion over the period. By contrast, Belarus recorded 27.6% growth, while Bulgaria, Moldova and Ukraine saw smaller increases. The value of transfers of $10,000 or more to crypto services fell 17.4%, from $591.5 billion to $488.6 billion, according to the report. The value of smaller transfers to crypto services, meanwhile, rose 8.3%. These retail-sized transfers accounted for 13.1% of the value sent to crypto services in Eastern Europe, the highest share of any region studied and above the global average of 10.1%. Eastern European crypto activity by country, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report Polish crypto ATM activity grows Crypto ATM activity also increased across Eastern Europe, with transaction volumes nearly doubling from $17.3 million to $33.9 million. Poland recorded a 120% increase in ATM transactions despite a 5% decline in centralized exchange activity, with stablecoins accounting for roughly 90% of its ATM transactions. Chainalysis measures the crypto economy using inflows to crypto services, domestic transfers between personal wallets and cross-border inflows to personal wallets. The figures are measured in dollars, so cryptocurrency price changes can also affect the totals, according to its methodology. Related: OpenPayd secures MiCA license as stablecoin adoption grows in Europe Ukraine receives billions in stablecoins Despite the broader regional decline, Ukraine remained a major destination for stablecoins, receiving $12 billion in cross-border wallet-to-wallet transfers. Of that, $2.41 billion was in retail-sized transfers below $10,000, according to Chainalysis. Chainalysis also found that countries with larger Ukrainian populations, including prewar diaspora communities and refugees who arrived after Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, generally sent more stablecoins to Ukraine. Among the 36 countries studied across Europe and North America, Canada was the largest source of retail-sized, remittance-like transfers, at $359 million. Crypto transfers to Ukraine by diaspora population, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report A Chainalysis spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the cross-border flows were largely denominated in US dollar-pegged stablecoins, although the firm did not provide a breakdown by individual token. news.title: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines
news.summary: The Home Office has revoked approval that allowed footage from speed cameras to be used in evidence.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines
news.summaryTr: The Home Office has revoked approval that allowed footage from speed cameras to be used in evidence.
news.articleText: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines - Published Further problems with the accuracy of speed cameras on English roads have been uncovered which may have allowed drivers to slip through the cracks and escape fines. National Highways discovered issues with speed cameras last year, affecting 154 out of 400 cameras but, following an investigation, said it had found another fault on units monitoring roads including those running between Huntingdon and Cambridge. The Home Office has revoked approval that allows footage from the cameras to be used as evidence in legal proceedings. US firm Verra Mobility operates the cameras but National Highways said it will now end the contract. Roads minister Justin Madders said: "We can't take chances with this. "If we're going to prosecute people, we need to be confident the system is working as it should. That's why we've taken the action we have." In a statement, Verra Mobility said it "remains fully committed to delivering reliable, innovative technology that helps make roads safer". The fault affected all of the variable speed cameras on smart motorways, and a section of the A14 between Huntingdon and Cambridge as well as the A1 approach junction to the A14. A spokesperson for National Highways said that Verra's camera system had been selected on the basis that it maintained Home Office approval. The agency said that since that was no longer the case "we are ending our contractual relationship to use the cameras for enforcement". It added: "We are considering all further commercial and legal options that may be appropriate." The BBC has contacted Verra Mobility for comment. Madders said that the enforcement of speed limits continues to be conducted through a range of different tactics, including mobile cameras as well as marked and unmarked police patrols. But he admitted that the camera system will not be fully fixed until sometime next year. Rod Dennis, senior policy officer at the RAC motoring organisation, said: "Malfunctioning speed cameras on smart motorways do more than just let speeding drivers get away with breaking the law and endangering lives – they further undermine confidence in the very types of road we know drivers already have serious misgivings about." There are 4,000 cameras across the entire road network. In December 2025, National Highways, which runs England's motorways, blamed an "anomaly" in how variable speed cameras were interacting with speed limit signs on some A roads and motorways. For example, on a road where the speed limit increases, a driver may see a sign showing 60mph but the camera recording it may still be working on the basis of a previous 40mph speed limit. The fault led to 2,650 wrongful speed camera activations between 2021 and the end of last year. Those who had been wrongfully fined have been reimbursed. As National Highways continued to test the system, it discovered a further problem "relating to how some of these cameras may activate in specific and rare circumstances". It said that according to its calculations, "the circumstances in which the latest issue could occur are extremely rare, and there is no evidence to suggest it has impacted enforcement". Nevertheless, it said it was "taking immediate steps to ensure compliance is maintained at relevant locations". It said it would out further traffic officer patrols in place to monitor the sites. news.titleTr: Asgari ücret zammı enflasyonu geride bıraktı: İspanya'da yeni rakam belli oldu
news.summaryTr: İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı.
news.articleText: Asgari ücret zammı enflasyonu geride bıraktı: İspanya'da yeni rakam belli oldu - İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı. İspanya'da sol azınlık koalisyon hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücrete yüzde 5,3 zam yapılmasını onayladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bakanlar Kurulu'nun aldığı karara göre aylık brüt asgari ücret, 1 Ocak 2027 itibarıyla 1.221 eurodan 1.286 euroya yükselecek. Düzenlemenin yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsaması bekleniyor. Asgari ücretlilerin yılda iki kez tam maaş tutarında ek ödeme aldığı sistemde, bu ücretlerden gelir vergisi kesilmeyecek. Zam oranı enflasyon tahminini aştı Asgari ücrete yapılması kararlaştırılan yüzde 5,3'lük artış, İspanya Merkez Bankası'nın 2026 yılı için öngördüğü yüzde 3,9'luk enflasyon oranının üzerinde gerçekleşti. Zam oranı, ekim itibarıyla son 12 ayda kaydedilen yüzde 4,9'luk enflasyonu da geride bıraktı. Memur maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam İspanya hükümeti, yaklaşık 3 milyon devlet memurunun maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam yapılmasını onayladı. Sendikalarla daha önce varılan anlaşma kapsamında belirlenen artış, 1992'den bu yana memur maaşlarına yapılan en yüksek yıllık zam olacak. Sanchez: 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücreti artıyor Başbakan Pedro Sanchez, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücretinin artırıldığını belirtti. Sanchez, “Çünkü bunu hak ediyorlar, çünkü ülkemizin ekonomik başarısı aynı zamanda onların çabalarının da bir sonucudur” ifadelerini kullandı. Başbakan Yardımcısı ve Çalışma Bakanı Yolanda Diaz ise sol hükümetin 2018'de göreve gelmesinden bu yana asgari ücretin toplam yüzde 75 artırıldığını açıkladı. Zam için Meclis onayı gerekiyor Hükümetin onayladığı düzenlemenin 1 Ocak 2027'de yürürlüğe girebilmesi için Meclis Daimi Komitesi'nin önümüzdeki günlerde onay vermesi gerekiyor.

news.titleTr: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ta eş zamanlı kesinti: Milyonlarca kullanıcı etkilendi
news.summaryTr: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ın dijital hizmetlerinde 17 Kasım akşamı erişim sorunları yaşandı. Downdetector'a çok sayıda hata bildirimi ulaşırken, kesintilerin ortak bir altyapı sorunundan kaynaklanıp kaynaklanmadığı henüz netleşmedi.
news.articleText: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ta eş zamanlı kesinti: Milyonlarca kullanıcı etkilendi - Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ın dijital hizmetlerinde 17 Kasım akşamı erişim sorunları yaşandı. Downdetector'a çok sayıda hata bildirimi ulaşırken, kesintilerin ortak bir altyapı sorunundan kaynaklanıp kaynaklanmadığı henüz netleşmedi. Teknoloji ve hizmet sektörünün önde gelen şirketleri, 17 Kasım akşamı eş zamanlı erişim sorunlarıyla gündeme geldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Downdetector verilerine göre Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'a ait çeşitli dijital servislerde kullanıcılar tarafından peş peşe hata bildirimleri yapıldı. Kesintilerin Türkiye saatiyle öğleden sonra ve akşam saatlerinde yoğunlaştığı bildirildi. Gmail ve Marriott kullanıcıları erişim sorunu yaşadı Gmail kullanıcıları e-posta gönderme ve alma işlemlerinde aksaklıklarla karşılaştı. Dünyanın önde gelen otel zincirlerinden Marriott'ın rezervasyon ve giriş sistemlerinde de erişim sorunları rapor edildi. Apple Pay, iCloud ve App Store'da aksaklık Apple ekosisteminde de birden fazla hizmet kesintiden etkilendi. Apple Pay, iCloud, App Store ve Apple Destek hizmetlerinde oturum açma, ödeme yapma ve uygulama indirme işlemlerinde sorunlar yaşandığı bildirildi. Apple'ın resmi sistem durumu sayfası da iCloud hesapları ve giriş işlemlerindeki kesintiyi doğruladı. Microsoft 365 ve Outlook'ta yeni kesinti dalgası Microsoft servislerinde de 17 Kasım öğleden sonra ve akşam saatlerinde hata bildirimleri yeniden yükseldi. Outlook ve Microsoft 365 kullanıcıları erişim ve bağlantı sorunları yaşadıklarını bildirdi. Microsoft, geçtiğimiz hafta 12-14 Kasım tarihlerinde 74 ülkeyi etkileyen büyük altyapı sorununu çözmüştü. Kesintilerin ortak nedeni henüz bilinmiyor Şirketlerin teknik ekipleri hizmetleri normale döndürmek için çalışmalarını sürdürürken, yaşanan aksaklıkların ortak bir küresel altyapı sağlayıcısından mı yoksa birbirinden bağımsız teknik sorunlardan mı kaynaklandığı henüz açıklığa kavuşmadı. Kesintilerin nedenine ilişkin şirketlerden resmi açıklamalar bekleniyor.

news.titleTr: Carney looks to China as Trump tariffs squeeze Canada's car industry
news.summaryTr: The PM has suggested Chinese automakers could replace American ones in Canada - but some say that would not be easy.
news.articleText: Carney looks to China as Trump tariffs squeeze Canada's car industry - Published Canada's car industry has become one of the clearest stress tests for Ottawa as it grapples with US tariffs on the sector. Now Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that he is looking to China, where he is on a visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit (Apec), as part of the solution. But that avenue is not without controversy, and is once again drawing the ire of those close to Donald Trump. While in Cambodia earlier this week, Carney told reporters that Canada could turn to European and Asian carmakers to save its auto manufacturing sector if a trade deal with the US could not be reached. If Canadian auto workers are "not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities. "Canada's going to move forward either way," he said. He went on to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Tuesday for their second head-to-head in less than a year. The two talked of the importance of developing their relations, and Carney said they had agreed to further tariff cuts. Neither side mentioned vehicles specifically, though analysts suggest the issue will have been prominent in their minds. In January, Carney said that opening the door to China's electric vehicles, external (EVs) could result in investment into Canadian-owned companies and the creation of manufacturing jobs in the sector. American tariffs on imports of Canadian-made vehicles have led to thousands of job losses in Canada and anxiety over the future, as 90% of cars made in Canada are shipped to and sold in the US. At the same time, China has been eyeing Canada as a potential entry-point to the North American EV market. Earlier this year, Canada announced that it would let in 49,000 EVs from China at a low tariff rate, with plans to raise that quota gradually to 70,000 by 2030. The move was a significant break from the US, which tariffs Chinese EVs heavily to protect domestic manufacturing. Peter Navarro, Trump's senior counsel for trade and manufacturing, warned the prime minister against cosying up to China in a post on X, external. "Are u really threatening to play China off the US? This is offensive in the extreme," he wrote on Monday. "You should be far more worried China is going to eat Canada alive." His comments were reposted by Pete Hoekstra, the US ambassador to Canada. Chinese EV manufacturers like BYD and Chery have already been lobbying the Canadian government for market access. Last week, Canada's Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu toured a Chery plant in China, external. He told reporters afterwards that Canadians could expect to see affordable Chinese EVs in Canada by early 2027. These moves come as the toll of US tariffs on Canada's auto sector has become harder to ignore. Stellantis, a multinational car manufacturer that made models like the Dodge Challenger in Canada, recently announced it would sell its assembly plant in Brampton, Ontario. The facility had been idle since 2023 for a planned retooling, but what was supposed to be a temporary shutdown became permanent after Trump's tariffs. news.articleText: ABD'de peş peşe sistem krizleri: Şimdi de Ulusal Güvelik'in gizli iletişim ağı çöktü - ABD'de havacılık ve bankacılık sistemlerinde yaşanan kesintilerin ardından bu kez Ulusal Güvenlik Ajansı'nın (NSA) kurum içi iletişim ağı devre dışı kaldı. İlk incelemelerde siber saldırı bulgusuna rastlanmadı. ABD'de dijital sistemlerde yaşanan aksaklıklara bir yenisi eklendi. ABD Ulusal Güvenlik Ajansı'nın (NSA) kurum içi iletişimde kullandığı çok gizli ağ devre dışı kaldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle CNN'in beş kaynağa dayandırdığı haberine göre, ajansın kurum içi iletişim ağında kesinti yaşandı. NSA yetkililerinin sorunun boyutunu anlamaya çalıştığı belirtilirken, şu ana kadar bir siber saldırıya ilişkin herhangi bir bulguya rastlanmadığı aktarıldı. NSA ise kesintiyle ilgili henüz resmi bir açıklama yapmadı. Önce bankalar, ardından havalimanları etkilendi NSA'daki kesinti, ABD'de son günlerde yaşanan diğer sistem arızalarının ardından geldi. Bir gün önce Downdetector, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, US Bank ve Wells Fargo dahil birçok bankanın dijital hizmetlerine erişimde sorunlar yaşandığını bildirmişti. FAA arızası nedeniyle ülke genelinde kalkışlar durmuştu ABD Federal Havacılık İdaresi (FAA), geçtiğimiz cumartesi günü hava trafik kontrol merkezlerini etkileyen bir iletişim arızası nedeniyle ülke genelindeki havalimanlarında kalkışları durdurmuştu. Dört saatten uzun süren durdurma, 11 Eylül 2001 saldırılarından bu yana ABD'de yaşanan en uzun süreli kalkış durdurulması olarak kayıtlara geçmişti.

news.articleText: Valilik uyardı: İstanbul'da fırtına alarmı! Rüzgarın hızı 80 kilometreye ulaşacak - İstanbul Valiliği, 18 Kasım Çarşamba gecesinden itibaren etkili olması beklenen fırtınaya karşı uyardı. Rüzgarın hızının yer yer saatte 80 kilometreye çıkacağı, fırtınanın perşembe öğle saatlerinde etkisini kaybedeceği tahmin ediliyor. İstanbul Valiliği, kent genelinde beklenen kuvvetli rüzgar ve fırtınaya karşı vatandaşları uyardı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğünün son değerlendirmelerine dayandırılan açıklamaya göre, güney ve güneybatı yönlerden esen rüzgarın hızını artırması bekleniyor. 17 Kasım Salı günü saatte 30-50 kilometre hızla esen rüzgarın, 18 Kasım Çarşamba günü gece saatlerinden itibaren 40-60 kilometreye ulaşacağı öngörülüyor. Rüzgarın yer yer fırtına ve kısa süreli kuvvetli fırtına şeklinde, saatte 60-80 kilometre hızla esmesi bekleniyor. Fırtına ne zaman sona erecek? Valilik, fırtınanın 19 Kasım Perşembe günü öğle saatlerinde etkisini kaybetmesinin beklendiğini bildirdi. Valilikten çatı uçması ve ulaşım aksaklığı uyarısı Açıklamada, kuvvetli rüzgar ve fırtınanın neden olabileceği olumsuzluklara karşı vatandaşların dikkatli ve tedbirli olması istendi. Özellikle şu risklere dikkat çekildi: - Ulaşımda aksamalar - Çatı uçması - Ağaç ve direklerin devrilmesi - Soba ve doğal gaz kaynaklı zehirlenmeler

news.title: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9327-26 CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today released the agenda for an industry roundtable to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9318-26]. Among other topics, attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization, margin, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. “From the outset of my chairmanship, I have been clear the CFTC will promote innovation in our derivatives markets in a manner attentive to the nuances of these markets and the varied asset classes that underpin them,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.” View the full agenda here. This meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Dial-in information appears below. For the highest quality, select the number nearest your current location. - New York: 646-828-7666 - New Jersey: 551-285-1373 - San Jose: 669-254-5252 or 669-216-1590 - US toll free: 833-568-8864 or 833-435-1820 - US Spanish-language line: 646-964-1167 or 415-449-4000 - International Numbers - Webinar ID: 165 708 9557 - Passcode: 669856 Individuals with additional questions should contact [email protected]. The roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9318-26]. Among other topics, attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization, margin, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. “From the outset of my chairmanship, I have been clear the CFTC will promote innovation in our derivatives markets in a manner attentive to the nuances of these markets and the varied asset classes that underpin them,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.” View the full agenda here. This meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Dial-in information appears below. items.titleTr: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
items.summaryTr: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
items.articleText: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says - Published A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says. There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority. According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman. There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost. They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control. All settlements are illegal under international law. - UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements - Published2 hours ago Local Palestinians said that the events in al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Monday night began with harassment by Israeli settlers. Palestinian children threw stones, they said, and the settlers opened fire, killing Fadda al-Fahidat, who was 72, outside her home. Fadda's daughter-in-law, Nema al-Fahidat, told the BBC that she died from a single bullet wound to the head. "It destroyed her brain," she said. According to the Palestinian accounts, Fadda's son, Arafat, rushed to the scene in his car after hearing the news and collided with an empty Israeli settler car parked outside his family home, injuring settlers who were standing nearby. The settlers then fired more shots, they said, injuring several Palestinians, including Arafat. "My husband, when he saw his mother, was not paying attention. He crashed into the vehicle. The vehicle was empty," Nema said. "My husband got out of his car and tried to reach his mother and the injured young men. Then he was shot." She added: "We tried to gather the injured people and move them away from the settler. We brought them here. But he kept firing, firing, firing. Even after we had brought the wounded young men here and moved them away from him, he continued shooting." Nema said young Palestinians threw stones at the settlers after seeing what happened, but asked: "What can stones do against bullets?" The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle". Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat." Later, an Israeli military source said Fadda was shot by an Israeli civilian and that there was no evidence that she had been involved in the confrontation near her home. Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Israel's police force said it had opened an investigation, and that officers and forensic technicians had been collecting evidence and interviewing witnesses. The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement. Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents. A BBC team saw settlers at the end of the street where Fadda was shot on Tuesday, as well as Israeli flags flying from four of the houses that they had moved into earlier this month. In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent. The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident. Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now. It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank". The UK government announced on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
